title: Nobody Trusts the Security Questionnaire. We Rely on It Anyway.
description: This article discusses the widespread reliance on security questionnaires in B2B transactions despite their inherent weaknesses. It highlights that these self-assessments are distrusted by those who fill them out but accepted by those who receive them, creating a paradox where trust is based on unverified vendor claims. The piece emphasizes that security questionnaires capture intentions rather than verified controls, contributing to persistent third-party breaches. It advocates for shifting from self-reported answers to observable evidence and independent attestations to establish trust between companies.
